title: New Residential Sales (November 2026 data) — 10:00 a.m. ET, the residential series this calendar tracks nowhere
source: EST: census.gov/construction/soc/schedule.html, the Survey of Construction Release Schedule, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 59,625 bytes), terminal row "November 2026 | December 17, 2026 | December 23, 2026" under the column head "(17th Workday) Revised Building Permits - 8:00 a.m. / New Residential Sales - 10:00 a.m.". Corroborated by census.gov/construction/xls/historic_release_dates.xls (HTTP 200, 55,808 bytes, 515 rows 1984-01 → 2026-11), whose terminal row reads reference 2026-11 → New Residential Construction 2026-12-17, New Residential Sales 2026-12-23. Further corroborated by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet, whose 2026-12-23 10:00 row names "New-home sales" among that vintage's releases. Filed estimate per the lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep; the sources are Census primaries and this id's own initial research should promote it. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the housing-starts-2026-12-17 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), six days past the proposer's own date. It is NOT a routine edition of a tracked series — it is a series this calendar tracks nowhere, which is the criterion the existing-home-sales-2026-12-09 and pending-home-sales-2026-12-17 lanes both set when they DECLINED routine monthly editions. Three reasons it earns a row. (1) It closes the residential set: this calendar now carries existing-home sales (12-09), pending-home sales (12-17) and housing starts (12-17), and new-home sales is the fourth and the only one with no entry. (2) It feeds a NAMED GDPNow expenditure leaf, which its proposer does not: the Residential sheet routes `valNewHomeSales` into `FRSBKX_USNAqtr` ("Brokerage commissions") as the other half of `valTotalHomeSales` alongside `valExHomeSales`, so the 12-09 and 12-23 prints move ONE line between them — the existing-home lane measured 140 vintages of it at a median 0.0376pp. The Atlanta Fed's workbook names new-home sales in 42 distinct shared strings, more than housing starts' 34 and nearly double existing-home's 22. (3) It is the last Census release of 2026 and it sits TWELVE days past cr-expiry-2026-12-11, so it is the corridor's deepest test of a funding lapse on this survey — the same Survey of Construction whose 17th-workday column publishes it also publishes the proposer on the 12th, and this lane measured that survey's lapse response directly: 9 of 514 releases since 1984 slipped out of the month after their reference month and all 9 belong to a federal funding lapse. Impact LOW and symbols empty, matching every sibling residential entry: no house playbook is macro- or housing-keyed (re-grepped 2026-09-06, 0 hits), and the proposer measured the homebuilder-ETF open effect dead since 2016. NOT researched by this lane beyond the date and the wiring — a future never-assessed session owns the analysis, and should measure the new-home-sales vintages' own residential signature the way this lane did for starts. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
